newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Young Briton shot dead, another wounded, in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Young Briton shot dead, another wounded, in Israel.

text.p: A British hitch-hiker was shot dead and his girlfriend was wounded in Israel's southern Negev desert on Wednesday by a car driver who gave them a ride, police said.
They said the student couple, in their early 20s, had picked up a lift at a gas station in the Red Sea resort of Eilat.
They had stopped for a smoking break 120 km (80 miles) north of Eilat at about one a.m. when the driver pulled out a gun and shot them.
Police and soldiers were combing the area but a police spokeswoman said the driver may have fled to Egypt.
"We do not exclude the possibility that the car has fled to the south towards the Egyptian border and probably crossed it," the spokeswoman said.
The motive for the shooting, the second attack involving young British tourists in Israel in three weeks, was unclear.
Officials at the Soroka hospital in the town of Beersheba named the woman as Charlotte Gibb. Police said she was undergoing surgery.
The British consulate in Tel Aviv said the woman had injuries to the jaw and arm. It declined to identify the couple until both families had been notified but said the pair were university students.
Initial reports had said the couple, who were found by passing soldiers, had been in a taxi.
"We understand that they accepted a lift. It wasn't a taxi," British vice-consul Alistair Elder said. "They were travelling north when the driver stopped the car and subsequently shot both of them."
Gibb told reporters from her hospital bed: "We were having a cigarette outside the car during a rest in the journey. I saw flashes and he shot us."
Deputy police commander Dudi Cohen told Israel Radio that police were checking all leads but had little to go on.
"The description given by the woman is the only thing we have. It is a partial description, even 'partial minus'," he said.

Several teenagers among a group of visiting British school students were slightly injured in Jaffa last month by an Israeli Arab who rammed into them with his car and then chased them down a street brandishing a Samurai sword.
Police said the assailant, who was arrested at the scene, had been bent on avenging the pasting in the West Bank town of Hebron of a poster depicting Prophet Mohammed as a pig.
